_about: Acronyms judged CORE for a security learner although the course cards rarely or never use them: foundational terms any practitioner is expected to know. Our own judgment of the field, never a claim about what an exam asks. The build (acronymRank.mjs `core`) places each in the Core tier. Each entry: the acronym exactly as in the course list, and why.

core.TCP/IP: the protocol suite every network runs on
core.ICMP: ping and traceroute; common in scanning and floods
core.DHCP: how hosts get addresses; rogue DHCP and starvation attacks
core.NAT: hides internal addresses behind one public address
core.PAT: the everyday form of NAT on home and office routers
core.MTU: packet size limit; shows up in tunnels and fragmentation
core.SMTP: sends email; the base of email security
core.IMAP: the mailbox protocol most clients use
core.VoIP: voice over networks; its own attack surface
core.BGP: routes the internet; hijacks make headlines
core.URI: the identifier behind every URL; used in web attacks
core.RAID: disk redundancy, the first line of availability
core.SDK: toolkit apps are built with; a supply chain concern
core.VDI: hosted desktops, common in remote work
core.VPC: the private network inside a cloud
core.CSP: the cloud provider in the shared responsibility model
core.CASB: controls and monitors cloud app use
core.SIM: the card that ties a phone to a number; SIM swapping
core.NFC: tap to pay and badges; close range attacks
core.PII: personal data that must be protected
core.PHI: health data with strict protection rules
core.HMAC: proves a message was not changed, with a shared key
core.PFS: old traffic stays safe if a key leaks later
core.DHE: key exchange that gives forward secrecy
core.ECDHE: the key exchange in modern TLS
core.IV: the random start value ciphers need
core.GCM: authenticated encryption mode in modern TLS
core.ECB: the insecure mode that leaks patterns
core.RC4: broken stream cipher to recognize and avoid
core.PKCS: the standards behind keys and certificates
core.PEM: the most common certificate file format
core.S/MIME: signed and encrypted email with certificates
core.WEP: broken Wi-Fi security to recognize and avoid
core.TKIP: legacy Wi-Fi encryption to recognize and avoid
core.WPS: a weak Wi-Fi setup feature attackers abuse
core.PAP: sends passwords in clear text; to avoid
core.NTLM: Windows sign-in protocol abused in pass-the-hash
core.GPO: how Windows settings are pushed to many computers
core.AH: the IPsec part that proves integrity
core.L2TP: VPN tunnel usually paired with IPsec
core.PPTP: old VPN protocol to recognize and avoid
core.TOTP: one-time codes from the clock, as in authenticator apps
core.FRR: biometrics wrongly rejecting the right person
core.CSRF: tricks a signed-in browser into acting
core.DEP: stops code running from data memory
core.DLL: shared code libraries; DLL injection and hijacking
core.TTP: how attackers operate; the core of threat intel
core.ATT&CK: the common map of attacker techniques
core.STIX: the format for sharing threat intel
core.TAXII: the way threat intel is exchanged
core.IRP: the written plan for handling incidents
core.BCP: keeping the business running in a disaster
core.SAN: Subject Alternative Name: how one certificate covers several names
core.RA: Registration Authority: checks identity before a certificate is issued
core.PIV: smart card identity used for strong sign-in
